The Portal

Not a sculpture with a base. A universe with birds.

The Portal inverts the usual logic of sculptural hierarchy. The geode is not the support — it is the subject. The macaws are the frame. What you are looking at is an 80-million-year geological event, presented by two birds who have been perched at its rim since the moment Fabiano finished them.

I
Exposed geode interiorThe geode was cut and polished along its natural cavity axis — a procedure that reveals the interior without disturbing the outer crust. This is one cut. It cannot be undone or redone.
II
Gold-plated mount precisionThe sodalite macaws are secured to the geode rim with 18k gold-plated bronze mounts fitted at angles calculated to direct the viewer's eye into the crystal interior.
III
80-million-year formationThe amethyst inside the geode grew in a volcanic cavity over approximately 80 million years. The citrine core at center — the golden cluster — is a secondary mineral deposit that formed inside the amethyst. This configuration is geologically rare.
IV
Agate slab baseThe piece rests on a raw agate slab selected for its complementary mineral banding. The base is a second geological object in dialogue with the geode above.

Origin

Minas Gerais, Brazil

The amethyst geode at the center of The Portal was mined in Rio Grande do Sul, Minas Gerais — a deposit known for producing geodes with unusually dense crystal interiors. The citrine secondary deposit at the geode's center formed inside the amethyst cavity approximately 60 million years ago, making it a geological object within a geological object.
